title: First dictation after idle hears audio but transcribes no words
description:
Voicebar (~/Code/BubbleKeyboard, Android IME): the first dictation after the phone has been idle for a while often produces no words at all, while the next attempt works. Seen with ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime (possibly also Parakeet). Happens both when auto-listen starts on tapping into a field and on a manual tap of Voice.

Observed (2026-10-22, build 1.5.5 with the new "Connecting…" state and speech/mic logging):
- "Connecting…" showed only a fraction of a second, so the ElevenLabs socket opened quickly. The user started talking after it cleared.
- The waveform moved, so the mic was producing audio levels.
- No words ever appeared (no live draft, no pill text); the dictation timed out.
- Pressing Voice again right after: it listens and transcribes normally.

So this is probably not (only) the slow-first-connection problem fixed earlier today (silence countdown now starts at the recognizer's ready signal; finishing before connection waits up to 8 s; keyboard-open warm-up; 3 s connect timeout).

Suspects, most likely first:
1. Voice filter: "Only my voice" / "Ignore children's voices" (VoiceFilterTranscriber). The waveform level is measured BEFORE the filter (MicRecorder → onLevel), but the recognizer gets the filtered audio. VoiceGate replaces blocks it judges "not the user" with zeros; its embedding model loads lazily on first use. A cold first run could be zeroing everything. Check for "filter: silenced a stretch" log lines and whether the filter is on.
2. ElevenLabs receives audio but returns empty partials (e.g. bad first chunk, previous_text lead-in, keyterms param), or an error / session message that is parsed as Other and ignored. No log of message types or bytes sent yet.
3. Words arrive but aren't shown: auto-listen guard holding live text until "engaged"; LiveTyper never confirmed; the pill not showing partials while voiceInField is true.
4. Mic contention with the wake-word listener ("Voice bar, listen anytime"), whose AudioRecord is released asynchronously: levels come from our recorder, but check that the recorder whose chunks are sent is the one producing audio.

Diagnostics already in place (Settings ▸ Logs, last 5 min): speech (connected in N ms, first words back, ended with no words back, warm-up), mic (first 2 s peak level), filter (silenced a stretch), dictation start line (auto/live/toClipboard).
To add: count of audio bytes actually sent per session; ElevenLabs message types received (session_started, partial empty vs non-empty, errors); whether the voice filter is active and its per-block verdicts on the first stretch; whether the guard engaged.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified from logs or a reproduction; the first dictation after a long idle transcribes like any other (live words appear within about a second of speaking); a regression test covers the cause; the logging added for diagnosis stays useful and quiet.
notes:
2026-10-22 (v1.5.6): root cause found by reading the dictation path, not from the logs — two defects in the auto-listen guard that together produce exactly the report (waveform moving, 'Connecting…' gone in a flash, no words anywhere, stops by itself, and the manual retry right after works).

1. Words were shown nowhere. With 'see what you say as you say it' on, VoicebarService set bar.voiceInField = liveTyping at the start of every dictation, and DockView won't draw the pill's text while voiceInField is true (the field is supposed to have the words). But an auto-started dictation types nothing into the field until the guard engages, so partials went to bar.showLiveText() and were never drawn. ElevenLabs could be transcribing perfectly and the screen stayed blank.

2. The guard often never engaged. AutoListenGuard.level() put loudSince back to 0 on any single chunk under the threshold, so engaging needed ~300 ms of unbroken above-threshold audio. Speech dips below it at every syllable boundary and plosive (a 6 dB dip is 0.15 of a level, and the threshold sits 0.15 under the user's usual level), so someone talking right at the phone could talk through the whole 8 s window and never engage it. The window then cancelled the dictation and threw away everything it had heard.

Why 'first after idle': the first dictation after picking the phone up is the auto-started one (tap into a field); the retry is a manual tap, which is engaged from the start and so never hits either defect.

Fixed: voiceInField now follows guard.typesLive(liveTyping), so held-back words show in the pill and move into the field the moment the guard engages; level() tolerates dips up to DIP_MS (400 ms) within a stretch of talking.

Also fixed WakeWord.Loop: it only checked 'stop' in its read loop, so being told to let go while the keyword model was still loading still went on to open an AudioRecord and startRecording() — taking the mic back a moment after the dictation had opened it (suspect 4).

Diagnostics added: one 'speech' line per session with the seconds of audio actually sent and a tally of what came back by message type (empty partials, committed, errors, session_started, 'not json'…), logged on cancel too (the guard cancels, so this path used to log nothing); 'filter' lines for how long the speaker model took to load and the first stretch's verdict either way; the guard's expiry line now says the loudest level seen, what it needed, and what it had already heard.

Not ruled out, left for the next report if it recurs: the voice filter zeroing a cold first stretch (suspect 1) and ElevenLabs returning empty partials (suspect 2) — both now visible in the log.
close_reason: Auto-listen held the words back and showed them nowhere, and the guard rarely engaged on real speech; both fixed, with the diagnostics asked for

title: Advanced speech isolation: engage auto-listen on whispers and soft speech
description:
Auto-listen engages only on loudness (within ~6 dB of the usual level for 200 ms, 8 s window), so a whisper or soft voice late at night can be transcribed perfectly and still be dropped. Replace the single loudness bar with weighed evidence plus a pocket veto: the box was tapped, explicit whisper detection (pitchless, high-tilted speech at syllable rate, confirmed by recognized words), fold open and held, held vs lying still, dark room lowers the bar, quiet voiced speech with the phone still counts against. Keep clearly heard words in the pill for a tap instead of dropping them at the window. Voice and whisper profiles. Everything in a new Advanced speech isolation settings group (Only my voice and Ignore children's voices move there).

Spec: openspec/changes/advanced-speech-isolation/ (proposal, design, 5 capability specs, tasks). Brainstormed 2026-10-23; design only, not scheduled yet.
acceptance_criteria: openspec/changes/advanced-speech-isolation tasks done and the change archived; a late-night whisper into a tapped box engages and types; room talk with the phone on a table doesn't; a pocketed phone never does; no sensors registered while idle.
